owned_statement_rows.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth $K$-scheme ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]) with sheaf of relative differentials $\Omega_{X/K}$ ([[def-sheaf-relative-differentials]], [[thm-kahler-differentials-existence-presentation]]) and derivation sheaf $\operatorname{Der}_K(\mathcal O_X)$ ([[def-derivation-algebra]], [[cor-derivations-represented-by-differentials]]).
For a coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]) the first derivative (extension) $\mathcal D(\mathcal I)$ is the coherent ideal sheaf generated locally, for generators $f_1,\dots,f_s$ of $\mathcal I$ on an open $U$ with local coordinates $u_1,\dots,u_n$ on $U$ ([[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]]), by the $f_j$ and all partial derivatives $\partial f_j/\partial u_i$.
Set $\mathcal D^0(\mathcal I):=\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal D^i(\mathcal I):=\mathcal D(\mathcal D^{i-1}(\mathcal I))$.
The ideal is generated by $f_j$ and their derivatives of order at most $i$ and is independent of the chosen generators and coordinates; for a marked ideal put $\mathcal D^i(\mathcal I,\mu):=(\mathcal D^i(\mathcal I),\mu-i)$ for $0\le i\le\mu$.
In characteristic $p>0$, ordinary derivations need not lower order: on $\mathbb A^1_K$ for a field $K$ of characteristic $p$, the ideal $\mathcal I=(x^p)$ satisfies $\mathcal D(\mathcal I)=\mathcal I$.

Let $(\mathcal I,\mu)$ be a marked ideal on a smooth $K$-scheme $X$ with $\mathcal I\ne0$ ([[def-marked-ideal]], [[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]), and let $0\le i\le\mu-1$ ([[def-ideal-of-derivatives]]).
In every characteristic,
$$\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal I,\mu)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\bigl(\mathcal D^i(\mathcal I),\mu-i\bigr),$$
and $\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal I,\mu)$ is closed. If $K$ has characteristic zero, or characteristic $p>0$ with $\mu<p$ ([[def-field]]), then the inclusion is an equality. In these same characteristics, for $\mu\ge1$ the condition $\operatorname{ord}_x(\mathcal I)\le\mu$ for every $x\in X$ is equivalent to $\mathcal D^{\mu}(\mathcal I)=\mathcal O_X$.

Let $(\mathcal I,E,\mu)$ be a marked ideal with $\mathcal I\ne 0$ on the smooth $K$-scheme $X$ ([[def-marked-ideal]]).
It is of maximal order if $\operatorname{ord}_x(\mathcal I)\le\mu$ for every $x\in X$; when $\mu$ is attained this is equivalent to $\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal I,E,\mu)=\{x:\operatorname{ord}_x\mathcal I=\mu\}$. For $\mu\ge1$, in characteristic zero or in characteristic $p>0$ with $\mu<p$, maximal order is also equivalent to $\mathcal D^\mu(\mathcal I)=\mathcal O_X$ ([[def-field]], [[lem-derivative-ideals-have-the-same-support]]).
Put $T(\mathcal I):=\mathcal D^{\mu-1}(\mathcal I)$ ([[def-ideal-of-derivatives]]).
A tangent direction of $(\mathcal I,E,\mu)$ on an open $U\subseteq X$ is a section $u\in T(\mathcal I)(U)$ of multiplicity one ([[def-order-of-an-ideal-sheaf-at-a-point]]): $\operatorname{ord}_x(u)=1$ for every $x\in V(u)$, so $V(u)$ is a regular hypersurface in $U$ containing $\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal I,E,\mu)\cap U$.
Such a $u$ is transversal to $E$ at $x$ if $u$ is part of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ compatible with the local equations of the members of $E$ through $x$ ([[def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors]]); the hypothesis is used only in the completion-automorphism and glueing lemmas.

Assume $\mu\ge1$ and either $\operatorname{char}K=0$ or $\operatorname{char}K=p>\mu$ ([[def-field]]). If $(\mathcal I,E,\mu)$ is a marked ideal of maximal order, then for every $0\le i\le\mu$, the derivative marked ideal $\mathcal D^i(\mathcal I,\mu)=(\mathcal D^i(\mathcal I),\mu-i)$ is of maximal order ([[def-ideal-of-derivatives]]).

(1) The characteristic-zero hypothesis is used in the proof at the existence of hypersurfaces of maximal contact. The recursive ordinary derivative operators satisfy $\mathcal D^i(\mathcal D^j(\mathcal I))=\mathcal D^{i+j}(\mathcal I)$ in every characteristic. What can fail in characteristic $p>0$ is order reduction: on $\mathbb A^1_k$, the ideal $\mathcal I=(x^p)$ satisfies $\mathcal D(\mathcal I)=\mathcal I$ ([[def-ideal-of-derivatives]]). Also, the top locus of an ideal of maximal order need not be contained in the zero locus of a single equation of multiplicity one; Hasse-Dieudonne derivatives occur in positive-characteristic maximal-contact formulations ([[lem-giraud-tangent-directions-and-controlled-transforms]]), but this remark does not claim that replacing ordinary derivatives by them alone yields a resolution algorithm.

Let $X$ be a smooth $K$-scheme, $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a nonzero coherent ideal sheaf and $E$ a finite family of divisors in simultaneous SNC position ([[def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors]]).
(1) The function $x\mapsto\operatorname{ord}_x(\mathcal I)$ is upper semicontinuous: for every $k\ge1$ the set $\{x:\operatorname{ord}_x(\mathcal I)\ge k\}=V(\mathcal D^{k-1}(\mathcal I))$ is closed ([[lem-derivative-ideals-have-the-same-support]]).
(2) The function $s_E(x):=\#\{D\in E : x\in D\}$ is upper semicontinuous and locally constant on the finite stratification of $X$ by the sets of members of $E$ through a point; for every $k$ the set $\{x:s_E(x)\ge k\}$ is a finite union of closed subsets, hence closed.
(3) Along the resolution algorithm the invariants of [[def-canonical-resolution-invariants]] are upper semicontinuous, being built from $s_E$, orders and the inductive invariants.
